In September 2023 we spoke, in the end, about one thing. Forty-five of us said "a government shutdown" by September 30. That same day, twenty-eight of us said "keep the government," twenty-five said "continuing resolution to," and twenty-five said "to keep the government." Twenty-four of us said "fund the government." Twenty-two reached "the government open," and twenty-one closed the phrase: "keep the government open." The convergence peaked on a single date, September 30, the deadline itself.

One phrase stood apart from the funding language. On September 29, twenty-two of us issued a "statement on the passing of." We do not, from this record, know whose.

None of these phrases began with us in this era; each first appeared in 2013. We report only that in September 2023 we arrived, together, at the same words on the same day.
